0.0.n: A set polite greeting used by staff to welcome customers.

1.0.n: This time word needs no particle here.

1.1.n: チェックイン plus polite します describes today's planned action, not necessarily something happening right now.

1.4.n: This polite ending follows the name; the speaker leaves out I.

2.0.n: With に, this indicates doing something before another action, here checking in.

2.1.n: This particle makes 先 describe when the luggage will be left.

2.2.n: Japanese does not mark this noun as singular or plural.

2.3.n: This particle marks 荷物 as what the guest wants to leave.

2.4.n: The plain form comes before こと and describes entrusting something to someone else.

2.5.n: This turns 預ける into an activity that can be discussed as a thing.

2.6.n: This marks leaving the luggage as the topic of the question.

2.8.n: This is the polite form of できる; verb plus こと expresses what can be done.

2.9.n: This sentence-ending particle makes the request a polite question.

3.0.n: This politely acknowledges the guest's request.

3.2.n: This formal service expression uses a polite past ending to show the request has been understood and accepted.

4.0.n: Together with ございません, this forms a very polite apology, literally saying there is no excuse.

4.1.n: This is part of ござる, a very polite equivalent of ある, used in the apology.

4.2.n: This is an incomplete piece of the polite negative ending ません, not a separate word.

4.3.n: This completes the negative ending ません; it is not a separate word here.

4.5.n: The prefix お adds respect when referring to the guest's name.

4.6.n: This marks お名前 as the information the staff member wants to ask for.

4.7.n: This asks the guest to repeat information already given.

4.8.n: This borrowed expression means the complete name, rather than just the surname.

4.9.n: This marks the requested format: the complete name.

4.10.n: This is the て-form of 伺う, which humbly describes the speaker's own action.

4.11.n: After a verb's て-form, も helps form a permission request: would it be acceptable if I ask?

4.12.n: よろしい is a polite alternative to いい, and でしょう makes the permission request less direct.

4.13.n: This ends the formal request as a question.

5.0.n: This reaction shows surprise or difficulty understanding what was said.

5.2.n: This is a hesitant start to saying フル, not a separate word.

5.4.n: The guest repeats part of フルネーム with questioning intonation to signal confusion.

6.0.n: This signals the staff member's realization that clarification is needed.

6.2.n: This refers to the booking associated with the guest's name.

6.3.n: This links the reservation to the name under which it was made.

6.4.n: The respectful prefix お keeps the clarification polite.

6.6.n: The staff member repeats this expression to clarify that the surname alone is not enough.

6.7.n: This specifies the format in which the name should be given.

6.8.n: With いたします, this forms a very polite way to ask someone for something.

6.9.n: This is the polite form of humble いたす, replacing する to make the request more courteous.

7.0.n: This signals the guest's response after the clarification.

7.2.n: This is the guest's surname, repeated before giving the full name.

7.3.n: This polite ending identifies the speaker by surname.

7.5.n: This surname comes first in the guest's full Chinese name.

7.6.n: This character is the first part of the guest's given name, 怡君.

7.7.n: This character completes the given name 怡君; it is not the Japanese name suffix 君 here.

7.8.n: This polite ending completes the introduction using the guest's full name.

0.tip: いらっしゃいませ is a standard staff greeting; customers do not normally say it back.

1.lit: Today, I check in. I am Chang.
1.tip: Japanese often leaves out I when the speaker is clearly talking about themselves.

2.lit: As for leaving luggage beforehand, is it possible?
2.tip: Verb plus ことはできますか asks whether an action is possible.

3.tip: かしこまりました is a formal way for staff to acknowledge and accept a request.

4.lit: There is no excuse. Would it be all right to ask your name once more in full?
4.tip: Verb て-form plus もよろしいでしょうか is a very polite way to ask permission.

5.tip: Repeating an unfamiliar word with rising intonation can signal that you need clarification.

6.lit: Ah, the reservation's name, in full, I humbly request.
6.tip: A noun plus で can specify the requested format, as フルネームで does here.

7.lit: Ah, I am Chang. I am Chang Yi-chun.
7.tip: 君 is part of this Chinese given name, not a Japanese title attached to it.
